examples.japanese: {全員|ぜんいん}が{賛成|さんせい}した。
{乗客|じょうきゃく}{全員|ぜんいん}が{無事|ぶじ}だった。
{全員|ぜんいん}{参加|さんか}でお{願|ねが}いします。
{試験|しけん}に{全員|ぜんいん}が{合格|ごうかく}するのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's difficult for everyone to pass the exam.

examples.japanese: チームの{全員|ぜんいん}が{一|ひと}つの{目標|もくひょう}に{向|む}かって{努力|どりょく}した{結果|けっか}、{優勝|ゆうしょう}できた。
examples.english: As a result of every team member working toward a single goal, we won the championship.

notes:
{全員|ぜんいん} refers to every single member of a defined group. Unlike みんな, it emphasizes completeness — no one is excluded.

USAGE:
Often used with が as the subject ({全員|ぜんいん}が) or as a noun modifier ({全員|ぜんいん}{参加|さんか}). Common in announcements, reports, and formal contexts. Can be used with counters: {全員|ぜんいん}で10{人|にん} (all 10 people).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全員|ぜんいん}{一致|いっち} (unanimous agreement)
- {全員|ぜんいん}{参加|さんか} (full participation)
- {全員|ぜんいん}{無事|ぶじ} (everyone safe)
- {全員|ぜんいん}{集合|しゅうごう} (everyone gather)
- {全員|ぜんいん}{合格|ごうかく} (everyone passes)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- みんな: everyone (casual, can refer to a vague group)
- {皆|みな}さん: everyone (polite address)
- {全|すべ}ての{人|ひと}: all people (broader, not limited to a defined group)
- {一同|いちどう}: all present (very formal, used in speeches and letters)
